Frequently Asked Questions

What is a token unlock in crypto?

Token unlock is a scheduled event where previously locked crypto tokens become transferable and enter circulating supply under a project’s preset rules. A token unlock schedule usually follows a cliff (a big one-time release) or a gradual schedule like linear vesting.

Why it matters for investors: unlocks make dilution predictable. If a large release is coming, the risk profile changes even when there’s no headline driving it.

How is vesting different from a token unlock?

Vesting is the rulebook for how tokens are earned or released over time; an unlock is the moment those tokens become tradable. In practice, projects can have tokens that “vest” but still can’t move until an unlock condition is met.

DropsTab reflects this separation: vesting schedules display the timeline over which token supply has already entered or is expected to enter circulation. Unlock events, on the other hand, indicate the exact dates when that vested supply becomes available, including the percentage of total token circulation being unlocked and the specific funding rounds involved, covering both past and upcoming unlocks.

What is an allocation, and why do investors care about it?

An allocation is a slice of a token’s total supply assigned to a group—team, early investors, community, ecosystem, treasury, and so on. Allocations matter because different recipients tend to behave differently once tokens become liquid.

On DropsTab, allocations appear as separate buckets on the vesting chart, so you can see which groups control most future supply and how concentrated the schedule really is.

What is TGE, and how does it affect unlock schedules?

TGE (Token Generation Event) is when a token is created and officially exists on-chain. Many vesting plans start counting from TGE because it’s a clear “day zero” for distribution rules.

A common point of confusion: TGE doesn’t guarantee tokens are tradable. DropsTab helps by showing which allocations are fully unlocked at TGE versus those still locked behind cliffs and linear releases.

What’s the difference between cliff, linear, and non-linear vesting?

A cliff means nothing unlocks until a specific date, then a chunk is released at once. Linear vesting releases tokens gradually in equal steps over time. Non-linear schedules release unevenly—bigger bursts at certain intervals, smaller ones elsewhere.

On DropsTab, these patterns are visible in the vesting timeline, which makes it easier to compare projects without digging through tokenomics PDFs.

What does the vesting chart show at a glance?

A vesting chart is a map of future supply by allocation bucket. Each row represents a group of holders, and the timeline shows when their tokens transition from locked to unlocked.

DropsTab makes the “past vs future” split intuitive: what’s already unlocked is effectively priced into circulation, while what remains ahead on the schedule is the supply risk investors still have to live through.

Why use a table to track token unlocks instead of only the chart?

Charts are great for understanding shape (heavy cliffs vs smooth releases), but tables are better for decision-making. An unlock table turns supply into a calendar: what unlocks next, when it happens, and how large it is relative to the token’s broader structure.

On DropsTab, investors use these tables as a quick filter so they don’t accidentally enter a trade right before a known supply event.

How do investors judge whether an unlock is “big” or “small”?

A practical way to judge whether token unlocks are “big” or “small” is to compare the newly released supply to expected market liquidity rather than relying on price charts. If the market can’t absorb the new supply comfortably, timing becomes a real risk variable.

This is why, on DropsTab, we measure several parameters to assess the magnitude of an unlock. First, we evaluate how many tokens are expected to enter circulation, expressed as a percentage of total supply. Second, we measure the monetary value of the unlock relative to the project’s total market capitalization.

Does it matter who receives the unlocked tokens?

Yes—often just as much as the amount. Team and early investors unlocks typically carry higher sell-risk than community or ecosystem allocations, simply because incentives differ.

DropsTab highlights recipient categories to help you assess this risk. In addition, we provide extra metrics to support informed decision-making:

  • Whether tokens have been fully unlocked for a specific recipient group;
  • If not, the percentage locked vs. unlocked;
  • The exact number of tokens allocated to that group;
  • The total value is currently locked in USD for that group.

This level of granularity allows you to evaluate not just when tokens unlock, but who controls the newly liquid supply—a critical distinction for short-term volatility and long-term tokenomics analysis.

What can this feature not tell you?

The limitation is important: unlocking and vesting data describes supply mechanics, not demand. It won’t predict the price. DYOR
